_comment: Known-good verdict per <skill_set>/<scenario>. CI fails a PR only when a cell recorded PASS here now fails. Regenerate with: python3 evals/compare_baseline.py --report <report>.json --update

current_pack/false-pass-validation.note: Observed PASS, FAIL, PASS on identical input, so this cell can block a pull request on noise alone. Deliberately NOT marked flaky: it is recorded PASS, and exempting it would drop a real check rather than fix it. Retry-once is what holds it — a single FAIL is re-run and only a second FAIL gates. Rewrite its checks, then re-measure with evals/flakiness.py.

current_pack/generate-semantic-layer-dp-.note: All ten checks assert on the CONTENT of files the agent writes, but the judge only ever saw a truncated transcript, so a correct file that was not echoed back graded identically to one never written — both runs failed 8/10 with reasons of the form 'the transcript does not show'. The scenario now opts into workspace_files, which quotes the produced files to the judge as ground truth. Kept flaky until a run confirms the verdict is stable on real evidence; the recorded PASS predates that change and is not trustworthy.

current_pack/nxd-setup-headless-auth.note: Returned FAIL then PASS across two CI runs of the same commit. The two agent answers were substantively identical — both ran whoami and told the user to confirm the displayed email; neither mentioned the 'Not logged in' caveat — so the flip was the judge splitting one check that bundled three separate requirements into a single boolean. That check is now split in two with the caveat dropped as a requirement. Kept flaky until a run confirms the split holds; re-measure with evals/flakiness.py before removing.
